Question: The solutions of the equation \[z^4 + 4z^3 i - 6z^2 - 4zi - i = 0\] are the vertices of a convex polygon in the complex plane. What is the area of the polygon?
Solution:
The coefficients suggest a fourth power. Expanding gives
\[
(z+i)^4=z^4+4iz^3-6z^2-4iz+1.
\]
Thus the given equation is equivalent to
\[
(z+i)^4=1+i.
\]
Put \(w=z+i\). This translates every vertex by the same amount, preserving area, so we can study the roots of \(w^4=1+i\).

Choose one root \(u\). It is nonzero because \(u^4=1+i\ne0\). Any root \(w\) satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
0&=w^4-u^4\\
&=(w-u)(w+u)(w-iu)(w+iu).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently every root is one of \(u,iu,-u,-iu\). These four numbers are distinct and all have fourth power \(1+i\), so they are exactly the roots.

Multiplication by \(i\) sends the point \((x,y)\) to \((-y,x)\), a counterclockwise quarter-turn. Therefore these four roots form a square centered at the origin. Let \(r=|u|>0\) be its center-to-vertex distance.

To find \(r\), write \(u=x+iy\), where \(x,y\) are real. The square-modulus identity follows directly from
\[
\begin{aligned}
|u^2|^2
&=(x^2-y^2)^2+(2xy)^2\\
&=(x^2+y^2)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence \(|u^2|=|u|^2\). Applying the same identity again gives
\[
r^4=|u^4|=|1+i|=\sqrt2,
\qquad r^2=2^{1/4}.
\]
Joining the center to the four vertices divides the square into four right triangles, each with perpendicular legs of length \(r\). Its area is therefore
\[
4\left(\frac{r^2}{2}\right)
=2r^2=2^{5/4}.
\]
Translation preserves this area, so the answer is \(\boxed{2^{5/4}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
